briefdescription.para: Holds the configuration entry for each CAN instance.

briefdescription.para: Initializes a XCan instance/driver.

detaileddescription.para: Utilized by XCan_Initialize() or XCan_VmInitialize(), depending on if Virtual Memory support is wanted or not.

The initialization entails:
Initialize all members of the XCan structure, except BaseAddress. BaseAddress should be taken care of by XCan_Initialize() or XCan_VmInitialize(), before they call this function.
Reset the CAN device. The CAN device enters Configuration Mode immediately after the reset is finished.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.
Pointer to the a configuration structure the XCan instance should be associated with.

briefdescription.para: Provides a stub handler for unset asynchronous callbacks.

detaileddescription.para: The stub is here in case the upper layer forgot to set the handlers. On initialization, all handlers are set to this callback. It is considered an error for this handler to be invoked.

briefdescription.para: Initializes a specific XCan instance/driver.

detaileddescription.para: This function should only be used when no Virtual Memory support is needed. To use virtual memory, the caller should invoke XCan_VmInitialize(). See the description of XCan_VmInitialize() for detailed information.

This initialization entails:
Search for device configuration based on the unique device ID/BaseAddress.
Initialize Base Address field of the XCan structure using the device address in the found device configuration.
Populate all other data fields in the XCan structure
Reset the device.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.
Base address of the device.

listitem.para: XST_DEVICE_NOT_FOUND if device configuration information was not found for a device with the supplied device ID/BaseAddress.

simplesect.para: In XSCT/classic flow, DeviceId is used to look up the device configuration.

briefdescription.para: Initializes a specific XCan instance with Virtual Memory support.

detaileddescription.para: This function should only be used if Virtual Memory support is necessary. The caller is responsible for calculating the correct device base address in Virtual memory address space and passing it into this function.

This initialization entails:
Search for device configuration based on the unique device ID/BaseAddress.
Initialize Base Address field of the XCan structure using the given virtual address parameter value.
Populate all other data fields in the XCan structure.
Reset the device.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.
Base address of the device.

Device base address in the virtual memory address space. The caller is responsible for keeping the address mapping from VirtAddr to the device physical base address unchanged once this function is invoked. Unexpected errors may occur if the address mapping changes after this function is called.

listitem.para:
XST_SUCCESS if initialization was successful.
XST_DEVICE_NOT_FOUND if device configuration information was not found for a device with the supplied device ID/BaseAddress.

simplesect.para: In XSCT/classic flow, DeviceId is used to look up the device configuration.

briefdescription.para: Resets the CAN device.

detaileddescription.para: Calling this function resets the device immediately, and any pending transmission or reception is terminated at once. Both Object Layer and Transfer Layer are reset. This function does not reset the Physical Layer. All registers are reset to the default values, and no previous status is restored. TX FIFO, RX FIFO and TX High Priority Buffer are also reset.

When an internal error requires a reset, the driver notifies the upper layer software through the error status code or interrupts. The upper layer software is responsible for calling this Reset function and then re-configuring the device.
The CAN device is in Configuration Mode immediately after this function returns.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.

briefdescription.para: Returns the current operation mode of the CAN device.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.

listitem.para: XCAN_MODE_CONFIG if the device is in Configuration Mode.
XCAN_MODE_SLEEP if the device is in Sleep Mode.
XCAN_MODE_NORMAL if the device is in Normal Mode.
XCAN_MODE_LOOPBACK if the device is in Loop Back Mode.

briefdescription.para: Enters a specified CAN operation mode.

detaileddescription.para: Allows the CAN device to enter one of the following operation modes:

listitem.para: Configuration Mode: Pass in parameter XCAN_MODE_CONFIG
Sleep Mode: Pass in parameter XCAN_MODE_SLEEP
Normal Mode: Pass in parameter XCAN_MODE_NORMAL
Loop Back Mode: Pass in parameter XCAN_MODE_LOOPBACK.

detaileddescription.para: Read xcan.h and device specification for detailed description of each operation mode.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.
Specifies which operation mode to enter. Valid values are any of XCAN_MODE_* defined in xcan.h. Only one mode can be entered at a time.

simplesect.para: This function does NOT ensure CAN device enters the specified operation mode before returns the control to the caller. The caller is responsible for checking current operation mode using XCan_GetMode().

briefdescription.para: Returns the Status Register value.

detaileddescription.para: Use the XCAN_SR_* constants defined in xcan_l.h to interpret the returned value.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.

simplesect.para: The 32-bit value read from Status Register.

briefdescription.para: Reads the receive and transmit error counters.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.
Receive Error Counter value after this function returns.
Transmit Error Counter value after this function returns.

briefdescription.para: Reads the Error Status Register value.

detaileddescription.para: Use the XCAN_ESR_* constants defined in xcan_l.h to interpret the returned value.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.

simplesect.para: The 32-bit value read from Error Status Register.

briefdescription.para: Clears Error Status Register bits.

detaileddescription.para: Clears Error Status bits previously set in Error Status Register (ESR). Use the XCAN_ESR_* constants defined in xcan_l.h to create the value to pass in. If a bit was cleared in Error Status Register before this function is called, it is not touched.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.
32-bit mask used to clear bits in Error Status Register. Combine multiple XCAN_ESR_* values with a bitwise OR to clear multiple bits.

briefdescription.para: Sends a CAN frame.

detaileddescription.para: First checks if TX FIFO is full. If not, it then writes the given frame into the TX FIFO; otherwise, it returns error code immediately. This function does not wait for the given frame being sent to CAN bus.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.
Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer containing the CAN frame to be sent.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if TX FIFO was not full and the given frame was written into the FIFO.
XST_FIFO_NO_ROOM if there is no room in the TX FIFO for the given frame.

briefdescription.para: Receives a CAN frame.

detaileddescription.para: First checks if RX FIFO is empty, if not, it then reads a frame from the RX FIFO into the given buffer. Returns error code immediately if there is no frame in the RX FIFO.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.
Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer where the CAN frame to be written.

listitem.para:
XST_SUCCESS if RX FIFO was not empty and a frame was read from RX FIFO successfully and written into the given buffer.
XST_NO_DATA if there is no frame to be received from the FIFO.

briefdescription.para: Sends a CAN frame through the High Priority Buffer.

detaileddescription.para: First checks if TX High Priority Buffer is empty. If yes, it then writes the given frame into the Buffer. If not, returns immediately. This function does not wait for the given frame being sent to CAN bus.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.
Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer containing the CAN High Priority frame to be sent.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if TX High Priority Buffer was not full and the given frame was written into the buffer.
XST_FIFO_NO_ROOM if there is no room in the TX High Priority Buffer for this frame.

simplesect.para: To send the frame immediately, without a delay from processor interrupt handling, disable interrupts at the processor level before invoking this function.

briefdescription.para: Enables individual acceptance filters.

detaileddescription.para: Up to 4 filters could be enabled.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.

Specifies which filters to enable. Use any XCAN_AFR_UAF*_MASK to enable one filter, and apply a bitwise OR to multiple XCAN_AFR_UAF*_MASK values if multiple filters need to be enabled. Any filter not specified in this parameter keeps its previous enable/disable setting.

simplesect.para: Acceptance Filter Register is an optional register in Xilinx CAN device. If it is NOT existing in the device, this function should NOT be used. Calling this function in this case causes an assertion failure.

briefdescription.para: Disables individual acceptance filters.

detaileddescription.para: Up to 4 filters could be disabled. If all acceptance filters are disabled then all received frames are stored in the RX FIFO.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.

Specifies which filters to disable. Use any XCAN_AFR_UAF*_MASK to disable one filter, and apply a bitwise OR to multiple XCAN_AFR_UAF*_MASK values if multiple filters need to be disabled. Any filter not specified in this parameter keeps its previous enable/disable setting. If all acceptance filters are disabled then all received frames are stored in the RX FIFO.

simplesect.para: Acceptance Filter Register is an optional register in Xilinx CAN device. If it is NOT existing in the device, this function should NOT be used. Calling this function in this case causes an assertion failure.

briefdescription.para: Returns the enabled acceptance filters.

detaileddescription.para: Use XCAN_AFR_UAF*_MASK defined in xcan_l.h to interpret the returned value. If no acceptance filters are enabled then all received frames are stored in the RX FIFO.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.

simplesect.para: The value stored in Acceptance Filter Register.

Acceptance Filter Register is an optional register in Xilinx CAN device. If it is NOT existing in the device, this function should NOT be used. Calling this function in this case causes an assertion failure.

memberdef.name: XCan_AcceptFilterSet

briefdescription.para: Sets the Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Register values.

detaileddescription.para: Sets values to the Acceptance Filter Mask Register (AFMR) and Acceptance Filter ID Register (AFIR) for the specified Acceptance Filter. Use XCAN_IDR_* defined in xcan_l.h to create the values to set the filter. Read xcan.h and device specification for details.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.
Defines which Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Register to set. Use any single XCAN_AFR_UAF*_MASK value.
Value to write to the chosen Acceptance Filter Mask Register.
Value to write to the chosen Acceptance Filter ID Register.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the values were set successfully.
XST_FAILURE if the given filter was not disabled, or the CAN device was not ready to accept writes to AFMR and AFIR.

simplesect.para: Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Registers are optional registers in Xilinx CAN device. If they are NOT existing in the device, this function should NOT be used. Calling this function in this case causes an assertion failure.

briefdescription.para: Reads the Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Register values.

detaileddescription.para: Reads the values of the Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Register for the specified Acceptance Filter. Use XCAN_IDR_* defined in xcan_l.h to interpret the values. Read xcan.h and device specification for details.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCan instance to be worked on.
Defines which Acceptance Filter Mask Register to get Mask and ID from. Use any single XCAN_FILTER_* value.
Mask value read from the chosen Acceptance Filter Mask Register after this function returns.
ID value read from the chosen Acceptance Filter ID Register after this function returns.

simplesect.para: Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Registers are optional registers in Xilinx CAN device. If they are NOT existing in the device, this function should NOT be used. Calling this function in this case causes an assertion failure.

briefdescription.para: Looks up the device configuration by unique device ID or base address.

In XSCT/classic flow, DeviceId is used to look up the device configuration.

briefdescription.para: Looks up the device configuration based on the device index.

detaileddescription.para: The table XCan_ConfigTable[] contains the configuration information for each device in the system.

parameterdescription.para: 0-based integer indexing all CAN devices in the system.

simplesect.para: A pointer to the configuration table entry corresponding to the given device ID, or NULL if no match is found.
